verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed zāqēn bāʾ bayyāmîm ... wəlōʾ yiḥam lô. 'advanced in days ... but he could not get warm' is exact; the ASV wording is only modernized.

Re-parsed yəḇaqšû ... naʿărâ ḇəṯûlâ ... ûṯəhî-lô sōḵeneṯ. 'Attendant' for the substantival feminine Qal participle follows the lexica and modern versions (NRSV, NJPS), and it is supported by masculine sōḵēn at Isa 22:15. The ASV 'cherish' rests on an obsolete derivation. The shift to direct address (bəḥêqeḵā 'your bosom') is kept.
naʿărâ yāp̄â bəḵōl gəḇûl yiśrāʾēl ... ʾăḇîšaḡ haššûnammîṯ: exact. 'Territory' for gəḇûl is a sound modernization of ASV 'borders'.
wattəhî lammeleḵ sōḵeneṯ wattəšārəṯēhû 'she became the king's attendant and ministered to him' is exact; lōʾ yəḏāʿāh keeps the sexual idiom 'know'.

MT short form ʾăḏōniyyâ is normalized to Adoniyahu, with the MT spelling in the note (shared names convention). miṯnaśśēʾ (Hithpael participle) 'exalted himself', the chariots, horsemen and fifty runners: exact.
wəlōʾ-ʿăṣāḇô ʾāḇîw miyyāmāyw 'had never grieved him in all his days' is accurate (ʿṣb 'pain, vex'). wəʾōṯô yālḏâ 'and she had borne him' renders the feminine verb more exactly than ASV 'he was born'.

wayyihyû ḏəḇārāyw ʿim 'he conferred with'; wayyaʿzərû ʾaḥărê is the pregnant 'followed and helped' (ASV). The MT short name form is normalized with a note, and tsade is written tz per the names entry. Non-blocking: in the note, replace 'as in wave A' and 'the draft's ts is normalized throughout the wave' with verse references (process language does not belong in published commentary).
The MT proper name wərēʿî 'and Re'i' is kept, and the Greek 'his companions' is recorded. That is a defensible MT-baseline choice for a construable text.

wayyizbaḥ 'slew' (ASV) is neutral between feast and sacrifice; 'invited' for qrʾ lə- is fine. Non-blocking: the book-internal rendering of zbḥ ('slew' here, 'slaughtered' at 19:21) should be unified in a later concordance pass, and 'wave A' in the note should become '19:21'.
wəʾeṯ-nāṯān ... lōʾ qārāʾ: exact, with the object fronted as in the Hebrew.
hălôʾ šāmaʿat kî mālaḵ ʾăḏōniyyāhû: 'has become king' (inceptive perfect) is more exact than ASV 'doth reign'.
ûmalləṭî ʾeṯ-nap̄šēḵ wəʾeṯ-nep̄eš bənēḵ 'save your own life and the life of your son': identical to the ASV and under the nefesh entry.
hălōʾ-ʾattâ ... nišbaʿtā laʾămāṯəḵā lēʾmōr kî-šəlōmōh: the oath-introducing kî is rendered 'Surely' (ASV 'Assuredly'), and the rhetorical question is kept. Exact.
ûmillēʾṯî ʾeṯ-dəḇārāyiḵ 'confirm your words' (ASV), with the literal sense in the note. Exact.
haḥaḏrâ 'into the chamber' (directional he); məšāraṯ participle 'was ministering'. Exact.
wattiqqōḏ ... wattištaḥû 'bowed and prostrated herself'; mah-llāḵ 'What do you wish?' is idiomatic. Exact.
nišbaʿtā bYHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā laʾămāṯeḵā kî-šəlōmōh ... : exact; 'YHWH your Elohim' follows the corpus convention.

citations: BHS apparatus ad loc. (many MSS, LXX, Tg., Vg. wəʾattâ)
verdicts.reasoning: Re-parsed MT wəʿattâ ... wəʿattâ: both are rendered 'and now'. The versional wəʾattâ 'and you' (ASV) is recorded. The MT is construable, so keeping it is defensible.
wayyizbaḥ šôr ûmərîʾ-wəṣōʾn lārōḇ ... śar haṣṣāḇāʾ: exact. 'Captain of the host' (ASV) keeps the ṣāḇāʾ link to 22:19.

wayyištaḥû ... ʿal-ʾappāyw ʾārṣâ 'with his face to the ground': exact.
ʾattâ ʾāmartā is formally a statement and is read as a question from context, as in the ASV and modern versions. Defensible.
kî yāraḏ hayyôm ... wayyōʾmərû yəḥî hammeleḵ ʾăḏōniyyāhû 'Long live King Adoniyahu': the jussive yəḥî licenses the idiom that the ASV brackets.
wəlî ʾănî-ʿaḇdeḵā ... lōʾ qārāʾ 'But me, even me your servant': exact.

Re-parsed ʾim mēʾēṯ ʾăḏōnî hammeleḵ nihyâ haddāḇār hazzeh (question). The Qere ʿaḇdəḵā 'your servant' is translated; the ASV follows the Ketiv ʿbdyk. The (ס) section mark is noted. Correct under the Ketiv/Qere convention.

Ketiv yhy (jussive) / Qere yihyeh. The optative 'may he be' is correct under either reading, given the following jussive wîḡaddēl.

wəhakkərēṯî wəhappəlēṯî are collective gentilics. 'The Kerethites and the Pelethites' is the standard rendering, here with the transliterated stem (ASV 'Cherethites'). The gentilic '-ite' rule is applied consistently (1:3; 2:7, 8).
qeren haššemen min-hāʾōhel ... wayyiṯqəʿû baššôp̄ār ... yəḥî hammeleḵ šəlōmōh: exact (shofar as v 34).
məḥallilîm baḥălilîm 'piping with pipes'; wattibbāqaʿ hāʾāreṣ bəqôlām 'the earth split' (Niphal bqʿ) follows the MT, and the LXX ēchēsen is recorded. Defensible.
wəhēm killû leʾĕḵōl 'as they had finished eating'; qôl haššôp̄ār; qôl-haqqiryâ hômê 'the sound of the city in an uproar' is closer than the ASV.
ʾîš ḥayil 'a worthy man'; ṭôḇ təḇaśśēr 'bring good tidings'. Exact.
ʾăḇāl 'Truly' (asseverative; ASV 'Verily'). Exact.
Exact; the gentilics are as in v 38.
wattēhōm haqqiryâ 'the city is in an uproar' (Niphal hwm; ASV 'rang again'). Exact.
wəḡam yāšaḇ šəlōmōh ʿal kissēʾ hamməlûḵâ 'sits' (stative). Exact.

Re-parsed yêṭēḇ ʾlhyk/[ʾĕlōhîm] (Hiphil jussive). The Qere ʾĕlōhîm is translated 'May Elohim make'; the ASV 'Thy God' follows the Ketiv. Anarthrous with a YHWH referent, it falls under clause (2) of the elohim entry. Correct.

paragraphs.text: וְהַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ זָקֵ֔ן בָּ֖א בַּיָּמִ֑ים וַיְכַסֻּ֙הוּ֙ בַּבְּגָדִ֔ים וְלֹ֥א יִחַ֖ם לֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: Now King David was old, advanced in days; and they covered him with garments, but he could not get warm.

notes.official: *bāʾ bayyāmîm* 'advanced in days' (ASV 'stricken in years'), the idiom of Gen 24:1 and Josh 13:1. *wəlōʾ yiḥam lô* 'but he could not get warm': the king's failing body opens the succession narrative and brings in Avishag, whose status becomes the pretext of 2:13-25.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֧אמְרוּ ל֣וֹ עֲבָדָ֗יו יְבַקְשׁ֞וּ לַאדֹנִ֤י הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה בְתוּלָ֔ה וְעָֽמְדָה֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּתְהִי־ל֖וֹ סֹכֶ֑נֶת וְשָׁכְבָ֣ה בְחֵיקֶ֔ךָ וְחַ֖ם לַאדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: So his servants said to him, "Let there be sought for my lord the king a young woman, a virgin; and let her stand before the king and be his attendant; and let her lie in your bosom, that my lord the king may get warm."

notes.official:
*ûṯəhî-lô sōḵeneṯ* 'and be his attendant' (ASV 'and cherish him'). *sōḵeneṯ* (also v 4) is the feminine participle of *skn*. The masculine *sōḵēn* is a palace official at Isa 22:15 ('this steward, Shevna, who is over the house'), and Canaanite glosses in the Amarna letters (*zukinu*) and Ugaritic *skn* name an administrator. The lexica give 'servitor, attendant' for the feminine (BDB; HALOT), and modern versions and commentators follow ('attendant', NRSV, NJPS; Cogan, *1 Kings*, AB 10, 2001). The ASV 'cherish' rests on an older guess and is not adopted (`sokhenet-attendant-1-kings-1`). Whether the word implies a recognized court position is debated; it bears on 2:13-25, where the request for Avishag is read as a claim on the throne.

*wəšāḵəḇâ ḇəḥêqeḵā* 'and let her lie in your bosom': the servants move from the third person ('my lord the king') to direct address.

paragraphs.text: וַיְבַקְשׁוּ֙ נַעֲרָ֣ה יָפָ֔ה בְּכֹ֖ל גְּב֣וּל יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וַֽיִּמְצְא֗וּ אֶת־אֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית וַיָּבִ֥אוּ אֹתָ֖הּ לַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: So they sought for a beautiful young woman throughout all the territory of Yisra'el, and found Avishag the Shunammite, and brought her to the king.

notes.official: *naʿărâ yāp̄â* 'a beautiful young woman'. The central `eshet-yefat-mareh` entry lists Avishag among the women of the biblical beauty formula; the full formula *yəp̄aṯ marʾeh* is not used here, so the entry's wording does not govern the line. Names: Yisra'el = Israel; Avishag = Abishag; 'the Shunammite' = of Shunem in the Jezreel valley (cf. 2 Kgs 4:8) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וְהַֽנַּעֲרָ֖ה יָפָ֣ה עַד־מְאֹ֑ד וַתְּהִ֨י לַמֶּ֤לֶךְ סֹכֶ֙נֶת֙ וַתְּשָׁ֣רְתֵ֔הוּ וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יְדָעָֽהּ׃

i18n.en: And the young woman was very beautiful; and she became the king's attendant and ministered to him; but the king did not know her.

notes.official: 'and she became the king's attendant' (*wattəhî lammeleḵ sōḵeneṯ*; ASV 'and cherished the king'), as in v 2 (`sokhenet-attendant-1-kings-1`). *wəhammeleḵ lōʾ yəḏāʿāh* 'but the king did not know her': *yāḏaʿ* in its sexual sense (Gen 4:1). The clause establishes that Avishag was not David's wife in fact, which 2:17-22 presupposes.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲדֹנִיָּ֧ה בֶן־חַגִּ֛ית מִתְנַשֵּׂ֥א לֵאמֹ֖ר אֲנִ֣י אֶמְלֹ֑ךְ וַיַּ֣עַשׂ ל֗וֹ רֶ֚כֶב וּפָ֣רָשִׁ֔ים וַחֲמִשִּׁ֥ים אִ֖ישׁ רָצִ֥ים לְפָנָֽיו׃

i18n.en: Now Adoniyahu the son of Chaggit exalted himself, saying, "I will be king"; and he prepared for himself chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him.

notes.official:
Names: Adoniyahu = Adonijah ('my Lord is Yah'); Chaggit = Haggith. The MT writes the short form *ʾăḏōniyyâ* here and at 1:7, 18 and 2:28, and the long form *ʾăḏōniyyāhû* elsewhere. The translation normalizes to the long form, as the Kings volumes do for Eliyahu and Achazyahu (2 Kgs 1:2-4), and records the MT spelling at each short-form site (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

*miṯnaśśēʾ* 'exalted himself' (Hithpael of *nśʾ*). *rekeḇ ûp̄ārāšîm waḥămiššîm ʾîš rāṣîm ləp̄ānāyw* 'chariots and horsemen, and fifty men to run before him': the retinue of a royal claimant, as Avshalom's at 2 Sam 15:1.

paragraphs.text: וְלֹֽא־עֲצָב֨וֹ אָבִ֤יו מִיָּמָיו֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר מַדּ֖וּעַ כָּ֣כָה עָשִׂ֑יתָ וְגַם־ה֤וּא טֽוֹב־תֹּ֙אַר֙ מְאֹ֔ד וְאֹת֥וֹ יָלְדָ֖ה אַחֲרֵ֥י אַבְשָׁלֽוֹם׃

i18n.en: And his father had never grieved him in all his days by saying, "Why have you done so?" And he too was very handsome of form; and she had borne him after Avshalom.

notes.official: *wəlōʾ-ʿăṣāḇô ʾāḇîw miyyāmāyw* 'And his father had never grieved him in all his days', i.e. never crossed or rebuked him (ASV 'had not displeased him at any time'). *wəʾōṯô yālḏâ ʾaḥărê ʾaḇšālôm* 'and she had borne him after Avshalom': the subject (Chaggit) is unexpressed. Adoniyahu was the eldest surviving son (2 Sam 3:2-4), the basis of his claim (2:15, 22). Avshalom = Absalom.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּהְי֣וּ דְבָרָ֔יו עִ֚ם יוֹאָ֣ב בֶּן־צְרוּיָ֔ה וְעִ֖ם אֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֑ן וַֽיַּעְזְר֔וּ אַחֲרֵ֖י אֲדֹנִיָּֽה׃

i18n.en: And he conferred with Yo'av the son of Tzeruyah and with Evyatar the priest; and they followed Adoniyahu and helped him.

notes.official: Names: Yo'av = Joab; Tzeruyah = Zeruiah; Evyatar = Abiathar. Tsade is written *tz*, as in Tzarfat and Tzidon (17:9) and in genesis-woh (Yitzchaq) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`). *wayyaʿzərû ʾaḥărê ʾăḏōniyyâ* 'they followed Adoniyahu and helped him' (literally 'helped after'). MT short form of the name, normalized as at v 5.

paragraphs.text: וְצָד֣וֹק הַ֠כֹּהֵן וּבְנָיָ֨הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֜ע וְנָתָ֤ן הַנָּבִיא֙ וְשִׁמְעִ֣י וְרֵעִ֔י וְהַגִּבּוֹרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר לְדָוִ֑ד לֹ֥א הָי֖וּ עִם־אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: But Tzadoq the priest, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and Natan the prophet, and Shim'i, and Re'i, and the mighty men who belonged to David, were not with Adoniyahu.

notes.official: Names: Tzadoq = Zadok; Benayahu = Benaiah; Yehoyada = Jehoiada; Natan = Nathan; Shim'i = Shimei. *wərēʿî* 'and Re'i' is otherwise unknown; some Greek witnesses read 'and his companions' (*rēʿāyw*), and a Shim'i son of Ela appears as an officer at 4:18. The MT proper name is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). *haggibbôrîm ʾăšer lədāwiḏ* 'the mighty men who belonged to David', David's elite corps (2 Sam 23:8-39).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּזְבַּ֣ח אֲדֹנִיָּ֗הוּ צֹ֤אן וּבָקָר֙ וּמְרִ֔יא עִ֚ם אֶ֣בֶן הַזֹּחֶ֔לֶת אֲשֶׁר־אֵ֖צֶל עֵ֣ין רֹגֵ֑ל וַיִּקְרָ֗א אֶת־כָּל־אֶחָיו֙ בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְכָל־אַנְשֵׁ֥י יְהוּדָ֖ה עַבְדֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And Adoniyahu slew sheep and oxen and fatlings by the stone of Zochelet, which is beside Ein-Rogel; and he invited all his brothers, the king's sons, and all the men of Yehudah, the king's servants;

notes.official: *wayyizbaḥ* 'slew' (ASV; also vv 19, 25): *zbḥ* is the verb of sacrificial slaughter, and a feast of 'sheep and oxen and fatlings' at a named stone may be a cultic accession meal, as at the renewal of Sha'ul's kingship (1 Sam 11:15) and Avshalom's sacrifices at Hevron (2 Sam 15:12). 'Slew' is kept as a neutral rendering that does not decide between feast and sacrifice; the same verb is rendered 'slaughtered' at 19:21, where the question is likewise open. *ʾeḇen hazzōḥeleṯ* 'the stone of Zochelet', 'the Serpent's Stone' (*zḥl* 'crawl'). Ein-Rogel = En-rogel, a spring south of the city in the Qidron valley (Josh 15:7); Yehudah = Judah.

paragraphs.text: וְֽאֶת־נָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא וּבְנָיָ֜הוּ וְאֶת־הַגִּבּוֹרִ֛ים וְאֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה אָחִ֖יו לֹ֥א קָרָֽא׃

i18n.en: but Natan the prophet, and Benayahu, and the mighty men, and Shelomoh his brother, he did not invite.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר נָתָ֗ן אֶל־בַּת־שֶׁ֤בַע אֵם־שְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הֲל֣וֹא שָׁמַ֔עַתְּ כִּ֥י מָלַ֖ךְ אֲדֹנִיָּ֣הוּ בֶן־חַגִּ֑ית וַאֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ דָוִ֖ד לֹ֥א יָדָֽע׃

i18n.en: Then Natan spoke to Bat-Sheva the mother of Shelomoh, saying, "Have you not heard that Adoniyahu the son of Chaggit has become king, and David our lord does not know it?

notes.official: Names: Bat-Sheva = Bathsheba; Shelomoh = Solomon. *mālaḵ ʾăḏōniyyāhû* 'Adoniyahu has become king': Natan states as fact what Adoniyahu has only proclaimed (v 5).

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה לְכִ֛י אִיעָצֵ֥ךְ נָ֖א עֵצָ֑ה וּמַלְּטִי֙ אֶת־נַפְשֵׁ֔ךְ וְאֶת־נֶ֥פֶשׁ בְּנֵ֖ךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

i18n.en: Now therefore come, let me, I pray you, give you counsel, that you may save your own life and the life of your son Shelomoh.

notes.official: *ûmalləṭî ʾeṯ-nap̄šēḵ wəʾeṯ-nep̄eš bənēḵ* 'that you may save your own life and the life of your son': *nepeš* in the idiom of saving one's life, rendered 'life' as in the ASV (`nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings`). Rival claimants and their kin were in mortal danger at a succession (cf. 2:22-25).

paragraphs.text: לְכִ֞י וּבֹ֣אִי ׀ אֶל־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד וְאָמַ֤רְתְּ אֵלָיו֙ הֲלֹֽא־אַתָּ֞ה אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ נִשְׁבַּ֤עְתָּ לַאֲמָֽתְךָ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בְנֵךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרַ֔י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֑י וּמַדּ֖וּעַ מָלַ֥ךְ אֲדֹנִיָֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: Go and get in to King David, and say to him, 'Did you not, my lord, O king, swear to your handmaid, saying, "Surely Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne"? Why then does Adoniyahu reign?'

notes.official: *hălōʾ-ʾattâ ... nišbaʿtā laʾămāṯəḵā* 'Did you not ... swear to your handmaid ...?': no such oath is recorded in 2 Samuel, and the narrative leaves open whether Natan reminds David or prompts him; many critics read the scene as a palace intrigue (Cogan; Sweeney, *I & II Kings*, OTL, 2007). The question form of the Hebrew is kept.

paragraphs.text: הִנֵּ֗ה עוֹדָ֛ךְ מְדַבֶּ֥רֶת שָׁ֖ם עִם־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַאֲנִי֙ אָב֣וֹא אַחֲרַ֔יִךְ וּמִלֵּאתִ֖י אֶת־דְּבָרָֽיִךְ׃

i18n.en: Behold, while you are still speaking there with the king, I also will come in after you and confirm your words."

notes.official: *ûmillēʾṯî ʾeṯ-dəḇārāyiḵ* 'and confirm your words', literally 'fill up your words' (ASV 'confirm').

paragraphs.text: וַתָּבֹ֨א בַת־שֶׁ֤בֶע אֶל־הַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ הַחַ֔דְרָה וְהַמֶּ֖לֶךְ זָקֵ֣ן מְאֹ֑ד וַֽאֲבִישַׁג֙ הַשּׁ֣וּנַמִּ֔ית מְשָׁרַ֖ת אֶת־הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: So Bat-Sheva went in to the king into the chamber; and the king was very old, and Avishag the Shunammite was ministering to the king.

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקֹּ֣ד בַּת־שֶׁ֔בַע וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַיֹּ֥אמֶר הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ מַה־לָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: And Bat-Sheva bowed and prostrated herself to the king. And the king said, "What do you wish?"

notes.official: *wattiqqōḏ ... wattištaḥû* 'bowed and prostrated herself': the paired *qdd* + *hištaḥăwâ* of formal obeisance (central `qadad-bow-the-head-paired-prostration-formula` cites this verse; its Gen 43:28 wording 'bowed the head' is not imported). *mah-llāḵ* 'What do you wish?', literally 'What to you?'.

paragraphs.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר ל֗וֹ אֲדֹנִי֙ אַתָּ֨ה נִשְׁבַּ֜עְתָּ בַּֽיהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֶ֙יךָ֙ לַֽאֲמָתֶ֔ךָ כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֥ה בְנֵ֖ךְ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרָ֑י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִֽי׃

i18n.en: And she said to him, "My lord, you swore by YHWH your Elohim to your handmaid, saying, 'Surely Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne.'

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֕ה הִנֵּ֥ה אֲדֹנִיָּ֖ה מָלָ֑ךְ וְעַתָּ֛ה אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ לֹ֥א יָדָֽעְתָּ׃

i18n.en: And now, behold, Adoniyahu reigns; and now, my lord the king, you do not know it.

notes.official: MT *wəʿattâ hinnēh ʾăḏōniyyâ mālāḵ wəʿattâ ʾăḏōnî hammeleḵ lōʾ yāḏāʿtā* has 'and now' twice. Many Hebrew manuscripts, the LXX, Targum and Vulgate read the second as *wəʾattâ* 'and you', which the ASV follows ('and thou, my lord the king, knowest it not'). The difference is one letter (ʿayin / aleph). The MT is construable and is kept, with the versional reading recorded (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`). MT short form of the name, normalized (v 5).

paragraphs.text: וַ֠יִּזְבַּח שׁ֥וֹר וּֽמְרִיא־וְצֹאן֮ לָרֹב֒ וַיִּקְרָא֙ לְכָל־בְּנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וּלְאֶבְיָתָר֙ הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וּלְיֹאָ֖ב שַׂ֣ר הַצָּבָ֑א וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה עַבְדְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א קָרָֽא׃

i18n.en: And he has slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the sons of the king, and Evyatar the priest, and Yo'av the captain of the host; but Shelomoh your servant he has not invited.

notes.official: *śar haṣṣāḇāʾ* 'the captain of the host' (ASV): *ṣāḇāʾ* is the army (also 1:25; 2:5, 32, 35), and 'commander of the army' (NRSV) is the sense. 'Host' is kept because the same noun names the heavenly retinue at 22:19 ('all the host of the heavens'), and the English keeps the lexical link the Hebrew makes.

paragraphs.text: וְאַתָּה֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ עֵינֵ֥י כָל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל עָלֶ֑יךָ לְהַגִּ֣יד לָהֶ֔ם מִ֗י יֵשֵׁ֛ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרָֽיו׃

i18n.en: And you, my lord the king, the eyes of all Yisra'el are upon you, that you should tell them who shall sit on the throne of my lord the king after him.

paragraphs.text: וְהָיָ֕ה כִּשְׁכַ֥ב אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עִם־אֲבֹתָ֑יו וְהָיִ֗יתִי אֲנִ֛י וּבְנִ֥י שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה חַטָּאִֽים׃

i18n.en: Otherwise it will come to pass, when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers, that I and my son Shelomoh will be counted offenders."

notes.official: *kiškaḇ ʾăḏōnî-hammeleḵ ʿim-ʾăḇōṯāyw* 'when my lord the king sleeps with his fathers': the royal death formula (central `shakhav-im-avotav-death-formula`, which cites this verse; also 2:10; 22:40, 51). *ḥaṭṭāʾîm* 'offenders', those counted guilty, i.e. treated as rebels.

paragraphs.text: וְהִנֵּ֛ה עוֹדֶ֥נָּה מְדַבֶּ֖רֶת עִם־הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וְנָתָ֥ן הַנָּבִ֖יא בָּֽא׃

i18n.en: And behold, while she was still speaking with the king, Natan the prophet came in.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּגִּ֤ידוּ לַמֶּ֙לֶךְ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּ֖ה נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֑יא וַיָּבֹא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֧חוּ לַמֶּ֛לֶךְ עַל־אַפָּ֖יו אָֽרְצָה׃

i18n.en: And they told the king, saying, "Behold, Natan the prophet." And he came in before the king, and bowed himself to the king with his face to the ground.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֮ נָתָן֒ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ אַתָּ֣ה אָמַ֔רְתָּ אֲדֹנִיָּ֖הוּ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרָ֑י וְה֖וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִֽי׃

i18n.en: And Natan said, "My lord, O king, have you said, 'Adoniyahu shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne'?

notes.official: *ʾattâ ʾāmartā* 'have you said ...?': formally a statement, read as a question from context, as in the ASV. Natan presents the feast as if it implied David's consent.

paragraphs.text: כִּ֣י ׀ יָרַ֣ד הַיּ֗וֹם וַ֠יִּזְבַּח שׁ֥וֹר וּֽמְרִיא־וְצֹאן֮ לָרֹב֒ וַיִּקְרָא֩ לְכָל־בְּנֵ֨י הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ וּלְשָׂרֵ֤י הַצָּבָא֙ וּלְאֶבְיָתָ֣ר הַכֹּהֵ֔ן וְהִנָּ֛ם אֹכְלִ֥ים וְשֹׁתִ֖ים לְפָנָ֑יו וַיֹּ֣אמְר֔וּ יְחִ֖י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ אֲדֹנִיָּֽהוּ׃

i18n.en: For he has gone down this day, and has slain oxen and fatlings and sheep in abundance, and has invited all the king's sons, and the captains of the host, and Evyatar the priest; and behold, they are eating and drinking before him, and they say, 'Long live King Adoniyahu.'

notes.official: *yəḥî hammeleḵ ʾăḏōniyyāhû* 'Long live King Adoniyahu': the acclamation formula (also vv 31, 34, 39); KJV 'God save king Adonijah' supplies a word not in the Hebrew. *śārê haṣṣāḇāʾ* 'the captains of the host' (v 19).

paragraphs.text: וְלִ֣י אֲנִֽי־עַ֠בְדֶּךָ וּלְצָדֹ֨ק הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְלִבְנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֛ע וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֥ה עַבְדְּךָ֖ לֹ֥א קָרָֽא׃

i18n.en: But me, even me your servant, and Tzadoq the priest, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and your servant Shelomoh, he has not invited.

paragraphs.text: אִ֗ם מֵאֵת֙ אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ נִהְיָ֖ה הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֤א הוֹדַ֙עְתָּ֙ אֶֽת־עבדיך [עַבְדְּךָ֔] מִ֗י יֵשֵׁ֛ב עַל־כִּסֵּ֥א אֲדֹנִֽי־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ אַחֲרָֽיו׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Has this thing been done by my lord the king, and you have not made known to your servant who should sit on the throne of my lord the king after him?"

notes.official: Ketiv *ʿbdyk* 'your servants', Qere *ʿaḇdəḵā* 'your servant' (Natan himself). The Qere is translated (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`); the ASV follows the Ketiv ('thy servants'). The Masoretic section mark (ס) closes Natan's speech.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַן הַמֶּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ וַיֹּ֔אמֶר קִרְאוּ־לִ֖י לְבַת־שָׁ֑בַע וַתָּבֹא֙ לִפְנֵ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ וַֽתַּעֲמֹ֖ד לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: Then King David answered and said, "Call Bat-Sheva to me." And she came into the king's presence and stood before the king.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשָּׁבַ֥ע הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר חַי־יְהוָ֕ה אֲשֶׁר־פָּדָ֥ה אֶת־נַפְשִׁ֖י מִכָּל־צָרָֽה׃

i18n.en: And the king swore and said, "As YHWH lives, who has redeemed my life out of all distress,

notes.official: *ḥay-YHWH ʾăšer-pāḏâ ʾeṯ-nap̄šî mikkol-ṣārâ* 'As YHWH lives, who has redeemed my life out of all distress': the Israelite oath formula (`chei-x-oath-by-the-life-formula`, which cites this verse), with the relative clause of David's oath at 2 Sam 4:9. *nap̄šî* 'my life' (ASV 'my soul') is the idiom of rescue from danger; `nefesh-scope-and-spelling-kings` reserves the transliteration 'nefesh' for the life that departs and returns (17:21-22) and keeps the dualist 'soul' out of the Kings line (cf. central `nefesh-chayah`).

paragraphs.text: כִּ֡י כַּאֲשֶׁר֩ נִשְׁבַּ֨עְתִּי לָ֜ךְ בַּיהוָ֨ה אֱלֹהֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר כִּֽי־שְׁלֹמֹ֤ה בְנֵךְ֙ יִמְלֹ֣ךְ אַחֲרַ֔י וְה֛וּא יֵשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֖י תַּחְתָּ֑י כִּ֛י כֵּ֥ן אֶעֱשֶׂ֖ה הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה׃

i18n.en: as I swore to you by YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, saying, 'Surely Shelomoh your son shall reign after me, and he shall sit on my throne in my place,' so will I do this day."

notes.official: *bYHWH ʾĕlōhê yiśrāʾēl* 'by YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (central `elohei-yisrael`). *kî kēn ʾeʿĕśeh hayyôm hazzeh* 'so will I do this day': the oath is carried out the same day (v 48).

paragraphs.text: וַתִּקֹּ֨ד בַּת־שֶׁ֤בַע אַפַּ֙יִם֙ אֶ֔רֶץ וַתִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֑לֶךְ וַתֹּ֕אמֶר יְחִ֗י אֲדֹנִ֛י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִ֖ד לְעֹלָֽם׃ (פ)

i18n.en: Then Bat-Sheva bowed with her face to the earth and prostrated herself to the king, and said, "May my lord King David live forever."

notes.official: *yəḥî ʾăḏōnî hammeleḵ dāwiḏ ləʿōlām* 'May my lord King David live forever', the court formula of Neh 2:3 and Dan 2:4, answering David's oath. *ʾappayim ʾereṣ* 'with her face to the earth': the physical ground, so 'earth' is kept and the central `eretz` default ('land') does not apply. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) follows.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֗ד קִרְאוּ־לִ֞י לְצָד֤וֹק הַכֹּהֵן֙ וּלְנָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֔יא וְלִבְנָיָ֖הוּ בֶּן־יְהוֹיָדָ֑ע וַיָּבֹ֖אוּ לִפְנֵ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And King David said, "Call to me Tzadoq the priest, and Natan the prophet, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada." And they came before the king.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר הַמֶּ֜לֶךְ לָהֶ֗ם קְח֤וּ עִמָּכֶם֙ אֶת־עַבְדֵ֣י אֲדֹנֵיכֶ֔ם וְהִרְכַּבְתֶּם֙ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בְנִ֔י עַל־הַפִּרְדָּ֖ה אֲשֶׁר־לִ֑י וְהוֹרַדְתֶּ֥ם אֹת֖וֹ אֶל־גִּחֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: And the king said to them, "Take with you the servants of your lord, and cause Shelomoh my son to ride on my own mule, and bring him down to Gihon;

notes.official: *ʿal-happirdâ ʾăšer-lî* 'on my own mule': the royal mount (cf. 2 Sam 13:29; 18:9); riding the king's own animal in public marks the designated heir. Gihon = the spring below the City of David (2 Chr 32:30), spelled as the Eden river of Gen 2:13 in genesis-woh.

paragraphs.text: וּמָשַׁ֣ח אֹת֣וֹ שָׁ֠ם צָד֨וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְנָתָ֧ן הַנָּבִ֛יא לְמֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל וּתְקַעְתֶּם֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַאֲמַרְתֶּ֕ם יְחִ֖י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

i18n.en: and let Tzadoq the priest and Natan the prophet anoint him there king over Yisra'el; and blow the shofar, and say, 'Long live King Shelomoh.'

notes.official: *ûmāšaḥ ʾōṯô šām* 'and let ... anoint him there': priest and prophet anoint together. *ûṯəqaʿtem baššôp̄ār* 'and blow the shofar' (ASV 'trumpet'; NJPS 'horn'). The *šôp̄ār* is the ram's horn, the acclamation signal of accession (2 Sam 15:10; 2 Kgs 9:13); Kings uses the metal trumpet *ḥăṣōṣərâ* separately at another accession (2 Kgs 11:14), so the two instruments are distinct in the same book. 'Shofar' follows exodus-woh, which keeps the word at Sinai (EXO-WOH-19:16, 19; 20:18) (`shofar-coronation-signal-1-kings-1`).

paragraphs.text: וַעֲלִיתֶ֣ם אַחֲרָ֗יו וּבָא֙ וְיָשַׁ֣ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֔י וְה֥וּא יִמְלֹ֖ךְ תַּחְתָּ֑י וְאֹת֤וֹ צִוִּ֙יתִי֙ לִֽהְי֣וֹת נָגִ֔יד עַל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל וְעַל־יְהוּדָֽה׃

i18n.en: Then you shall come up after him, and he shall come and sit on my throne; for he shall be king in my place; and I have appointed him to be prince over Yisra'el and over Yehudah."

notes.official: *nāḡîḏ* 'prince' (ASV): the designated ruler, the title given to Sha'ul and David at their designation (1 Sam 9:16; 10:1; 13:14; 2 Sam 5:2; 7:8). It is a title of appointment rather than of birth ('leader-designate', BDB; HALOT); 'prince' is kept with that sense recorded here. 'over Yisra'el and over Yehudah': the two parts of the Davidic realm named separately.

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֨עַן בְּנָיָ֧הוּ בֶן־יְהֽוֹיָדָ֛ע אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּ֣אמֶר ׀ אָמֵ֑ן כֵּ֚ן יֹאמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה אֱלֹהֵ֖י אֲדֹנִ֥י הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: And Benayahu the son of Yehoyada answered the king and said, "Amen; so may YHWH, the Elohim of my lord the king, say.

notes.official: *ʾāmēn kēn yōʾmar YHWH* 'Amen; so may YHWH ... say': a jussive confirmation of the king's word.

paragraphs.text: כַּאֲשֶׁ֨ר הָיָ֤ה יְהוָה֙ עִם־אֲדֹנִ֣י הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ כֵּ֖ן יהי [יִֽהְיֶ֣ה] עִם־שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וִֽיגַדֵּל֙ אֶת־כִּסְא֔וֹ מִ֨כִּסֵּ֔א אֲדֹנִ֖י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ דָּוִֽד׃

i18n.en: As YHWH has been with my lord the king, so may he be with Shelomoh, and make his throne greater than the throne of my lord King David."

notes.official: Ketiv *yhy* (jussive, 'may he be'), Qere *yihyeh* (imperfect). The Qere is translated; its optative force is carried by the following jussive *wîḡaddēl* 'and make greater', so 'may he be' renders the verse either way (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`). *kaʾăšer hāyâ YHWH ʿim-... kēn yihyeh ʿim-šəlōmōh* is the divine-presence formula (central `elohim-imkha-divine-presence-formula`, which cites this verse).

paragraphs.text: וַיֵּ֣רֶד צָד֣וֹק הַ֠כֹּהֵן וְנָתָ֨ן הַנָּבִ֜יא וּבְנָיָ֣הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֗ע וְהַכְּרֵתִי֙ וְהַפְּלֵתִ֔י וַיַּרְכִּ֙בוּ֙ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַל־פִּרְדַּ֖ת הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֑ד וַיֹּלִ֥כוּ אֹת֖וֹ עַל־גִּחֽוֹן׃

i18n.en: So Tzadoq the priest, and Natan the prophet, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites went down, and caused Shelomoh to ride on King David's mule, and brought him to Gihon.

notes.official: *wəhakkərēṯî wəhappəlēṯî* 'and the Kerethites and the Pelethites' (ASV 'the Cherethites and the Pelethites'): David's foreign guard under Benayahu (2 Sam 8:18; 20:23). The singular gentilics are collective. 'Kerethite' is usually connected with Crete and the coastal *kərēṯîm* of 1 Sam 30:14 and Zeph 2:5, and 'Pelethite' is often explained as a variant of 'Philistine' (HALOT; Cogan). Gentilics take English '-ite' on the transliterated stem, like 'the Shunammite' (1:3) and 'the Tishbite' (17:1) (`hebrew-proper-name-transliteration-convention-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּקַּח֩ צָד֨וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֜ן אֶת־קֶ֤רֶן הַשֶּׁ֙מֶן֙ מִן־הָאֹ֔הֶל וַיִּמְשַׁ֖ח אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַֽיִּתְקְעוּ֙ בַּשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּֽאמְרוּ֙ כָּל־הָעָ֔ם יְחִ֖י הַמֶּ֥לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Tzadoq the priest took the horn of oil out of the Tent and anointed Shelomoh. And they blew the shofar, and all the people said, "Long live King Shelomoh."

notes.official: *qeren haššemen* 'the horn of oil': an animal horn used as a flask (1 Sam 16:1, 13). *min-hāʾōhel* 'out of the Tent', the tent David pitched for the ark (2 Sam 6:17), the 'Tent of YHWH' of 2:28. 'They blew the shofar', as v 34 (`shofar-coronation-signal-1-kings-1`).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּעֲל֤וּ כָל־הָעָם֙ אַֽחֲרָ֔יו וְהָעָם֙ מְחַלְּלִ֣ים בַּחֲלִלִ֔ים וּשְׂמֵחִ֖ים שִׂמְחָ֣ה גְדוֹלָ֑ה וַתִּבָּקַ֥ע הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּקוֹלָֽם׃

i18n.en: And all the people came up after him, and the people were piping with pipes and rejoicing with great joy, so that the earth split with their sound.

notes.official: *məḥallilîm baḥălilîm* 'piping with pipes'. *wattibbāqaʿ hāʾāreṣ bəqôlām* 'so that the earth split with their sound' (ASV 'rent'): hyperbole. *ʾereṣ* is the physical ground, so 'earth' is kept and the central `eretz` default ('land') is not applied (also 1:31, 52; 2:2). The LXX reads 'the earth resounded' (*ēchēsen*), which may reflect a different verb or a smoothing; the MT is kept (`mt-baseline-at-versional-cruxes-and-versification-kings`).

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע אֲדֹנִיָּ֗הוּ וְכָל־הַקְּרֻאִים֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֔וֹ וְהֵ֖ם כִּלּ֣וּ לֶאֱכֹ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע יוֹאָב֙ אֶת־ק֣וֹל הַשּׁוֹפָ֔ר וַיֹּ֕אמֶר מַדּ֥וּעַ קֽוֹל־הַקִּרְיָ֖ה הוֹמָֽה׃

i18n.en: And Adoniyahu and all the guests who were with him heard it as they had finished eating. And Yo'av heard the sound of the shofar and said, "Why is the sound of the city in an uproar?"

notes.official: *qôl haššôp̄ār* 'the sound of the shofar' (v 34). *maddûaʿ qôl-haqqiryâ hômê* 'Why is the sound of the city in an uproar?'; *qiryâ* is a literary word for 'town'.

paragraphs.text: עוֹדֶ֣נּוּ מְדַבֵּ֔ר וְהִנֵּ֧ה יוֹנָתָ֛ן בֶּן־אֶבְיָתָ֥ר הַכֹּהֵ֖ן בָּ֑א וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֲדֹנִיָּ֙הוּ֙ בֹּ֔א כִּ֣י אִ֥ישׁ חַ֛יִל אַ֖תָּה וְט֥וֹב תְּבַשֵּֽׂר׃

i18n.en: While he was still speaking, behold, Yonatan the son of Evyatar the priest came; and Adoniyahu said, "Come in, for you are a worthy man and bring good tidings."

notes.official: Yonatan = Jonathan. *ʾîš ḥayil* 'a worthy man': *ḥayil* covers strength, capacity and standing; Shelomoh uses it of Adoniyahu at v 52 (*ben-ḥayil*). *wəṭôḇ təḇaśśēr* 'and bring good tidings' (*bśr*, the verb of the bearer of news, 2 Sam 18:19-31).

paragraphs.text: וַיַּ֙עַן֙ יוֹנָתָ֔ן וַיֹּ֖אמֶר לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ אֲבָ֕ל אֲדֹנֵ֥ינוּ הַמֶּֽלֶךְ־דָּוִ֖ד הִמְלִ֥יךְ אֶת־שְׁלֹמֹֽה׃

i18n.en: And Yonatan answered and said to Adoniyahu, "Truly, our lord King David has made Shelomoh king;

notes.official: *ʾăḇāl* 'Truly' (ASV 'Verily'): an asseverative or adversative particle ('No, rather'); here it overturns Adoniyahu's hope.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח אִתּֽוֹ־הַ֠מֶּלֶךְ אֶת־צָד֨וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֜ן וְאֶת־נָתָ֣ן הַנָּבִ֗יא וּבְנָיָ֙הוּ֙ בֶּן־יְה֣וֹיָדָ֔ע וְהַכְּרֵתִ֖י וְהַפְּלֵתִ֑י וַיַּרְכִּ֣בוּ אֹת֔וֹ עַ֖ל פִּרְדַּ֥ת הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃

i18n.en: and the king has sent with him Tzadoq the priest, and Natan the prophet, and Benayahu the son of Yehoyada, and the Kerethites and the Pelethites; and they have caused him to ride on the king's mule;

paragraphs.text: וַיִּמְשְׁח֣וּ אֹת֡וֹ צָד֣וֹק הַכֹּהֵ֣ן וְנָתָן֩ הַנָּבִ֨יא לְמֶ֜לֶךְ בְּגִח֗וֹן וַיַּעֲל֤וּ מִשָּׁם֙ שְׂמֵחִ֔ים וַתֵּהֹ֖ם הַקִּרְיָ֑ה ה֥וּא הַקּ֖וֹל אֲשֶׁ֥ר שְׁמַעְתֶּֽם׃

i18n.en: and Tzadoq the priest and Natan the prophet have anointed him king in Gihon; and they have come up from there rejoicing, so that the city is in an uproar. This is the sound that you have heard.

paragraphs.text: וְגַם֙ יָשַׁ֣ב שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה עַ֖ל כִּסֵּ֥א הַמְּלוּכָֽה׃

i18n.en: And also Shelomoh sits on the throne of the kingdom.

paragraphs.text: וְגַם־בָּ֜אוּ עַבְדֵ֣י הַמֶּ֗לֶךְ לְ֠בָרֵךְ אֶת־אֲדֹנֵ֜ינוּ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִד֮ לֵאמֹר֒ יֵיטֵ֨ב אלהיך [אֱלֹהִ֜ים] אֶת־שֵׁ֤ם שְׁלֹמֹה֙ מִשְּׁמֶ֔ךָ וִֽיגַדֵּ֥ל אֶת־כִּסְא֖וֹ מִכִּסְאֶ֑ךָ וַיִּשְׁתַּ֥חוּ הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ עַל־הַמִּשְׁכָּֽב׃

i18n.en: And moreover the king's servants came to bless our lord King David, saying, 'May Elohim make the name of Shelomoh better than your name, and make his throne greater than your throne.' And the king bowed himself upon the bed.

notes.official: Ketiv *ʾlhyk* 'your Elohim', Qere *ʾĕlōhîm*. The Qere is translated; anarthrous, with YHWH as referent, it is 'Elohim' without the article (`ketiv-qere-qere-translated-kings`; `elohim-referent-and-article-conventions-kings`, clause 2). The ASV follows the Ketiv ('Thy God'). *wayyištaḥû hammeleḵ ʿal-hammiškāḇ* 'And the king bowed himself upon the bed', in worship (cf. Gen 47:31).

paragraphs.text: וְגַם־כָּ֖כָה אָמַ֣ר הַמֶּ֑לֶךְ בָּר֨וּךְ יְהוָ֜ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל אֲשֶׁ֨ר נָתַ֥ן הַיּ֛וֹם יֹשֵׁ֥ב עַל־כִּסְאִ֖י וְעֵינַ֥י רֹאֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: And thus also said the king, 'Blessed be YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el, who has given one to sit on my throne this day, my own eyes seeing it.'"

notes.official: 'Blessed be YHWH, the Elohim of Yisra'el' (central `elohei-yisrael`): the oath of v 30 fulfilled 'this day'. *wəʿênay rōʾôṯ* 'my own eyes seeing it'. The LXX reads 'one of my seed' as the object of 'has given'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֶּֽחֶרְדוּ֙ וַיָּקֻ֔מוּ כָּל־הַ֨קְּרֻאִ֔ים אֲשֶׁ֖ר לַאֲדֹנִיָּ֑הוּ וַיֵּלְכ֖וּ אִ֥ישׁ לְדַרְכּֽוֹ׃

i18n.en: And all the guests of Adoniyahu trembled, and rose up, and went each man his way.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א מִפְּנֵ֣י שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיָּ֣קָם וַיֵּ֔לֶךְ וַֽיַּחֲזֵ֖ק בְּקַרְנ֥וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּֽחַ׃

i18n.en: And Adoniyahu feared because of Shelomoh; and he arose and went and caught hold of the horns of the altar.

notes.official:
*wayyaḥăzēq bəqarnôṯ hammizbēaḥ* 'and caught hold of the horns of the altar' (ASV). The *qarnôṯ* are the horn-shaped projections at the four upper corners of an Israelite altar (Ex 27:2; 29:12), known from excavated horned altars such as the reassembled altar of Tel Be'er Sheva (Aharoni, *BA* 37, 1974). Grasping them was an act of seeking asylum, a custom regulated by Ex 21:13-14. The literal 'horns' is kept (new central `qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`). The altar is presumably the one at the Tent of v 39 and 2:28.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The Book Which Tells the Truth (ch. 3) cites this verse and 2:28 ('He caught hold on the horns of the altar') and reads the gesture as the handling of the levers of a transmitter-receiver used to contact the creators. The line renders *qarnôṯ hammizbēaḥ* literally, as every major version does, and does not encode that reading.

paragraphs.text: וַיֻּגַּ֤ד לִשְׁלֹמֹה֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר הִנֵּה֙ אֲדֹ֣נִיָּ֔הוּ יָרֵ֖א אֶת־הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וְ֠הִנֵּה אָחַ֞ז בְּקַרְנ֤וֹת הַמִּזְבֵּ֙חַ֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר יִשָּֽׁבַֽע־לִ֤י כַיּוֹם֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִם־יָמִ֥ית אֶת־עַבְדּ֖וֹ בֶּחָֽרֶב׃

i18n.en: And it was told Shelomoh, saying, "Behold, Adoniyahu fears King Shelomoh; for behold, he has laid hold of the horns of the altar, saying, 'Let King Shelomoh first swear to me that he will not put his servant to death with the sword.'"

notes.official: *hinnēh ʾāḥaz bəqarnôṯ hammizbēaḥ* 'he has laid hold of the horns of the altar' (`qarnot-ha-mizbeach-horns-of-the-altar-cross-corpus`). *yiššāḇaʿ-lî ḵayyôm* 'Let ... first swear to me': *kayyôm* 'today, first of all' (cf. Gen 25:31, 33). Adoniyahu now calls himself Shelomoh's 'servant'.

paragraphs.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה אִ֚ם יִהְיֶ֣ה לְבֶן־חַ֔יִל לֹֽא־יִפֹּ֥ל מִשַּׂעֲרָת֖וֹ אָ֑רְצָה וְאִם־רָעָ֥ה תִמָּצֵא־ב֖וֹ וָמֵֽת׃

i18n.en: And Shelomoh said, "If he shows himself a worthy man, not one of his hairs shall fall to the earth; but if wickedness is found in him, he shall die."

notes.official: *ʾim yihyeh ləḇen-ḥayil* 'If he shows himself a worthy man' (cf. v 42). *lōʾ-yippōl miśśaʿărāṯô ʾārṣâ* 'not one of his hairs shall fall to the earth' (1 Sam 14:45; 2 Sam 14:11). The conditional amnesty is the hinge of 2:13-25.

paragraphs.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֞ח הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֗ה וַיֹּרִדֻ֙הוּ֙ מֵעַ֣ל הַמִּזְבֵּ֔חַ וַיָּבֹ֕א וַיִּשְׁתַּ֖חוּ לַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֑ה וַיֹּֽאמֶר־ל֥וֹ שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לֵ֥ךְ לְבֵיתֶֽךָ׃ (פ)

i18n.en: So King Shelomoh sent, and they brought him down from the altar. And he came and prostrated himself to King Shelomoh; and Shelomoh said to him, "Go to your house."

notes.official: *wayyōriḏuhû mēʿal hammizbēaḥ* 'they brought him down from the altar': leaving the altar ends the asylum. The Masoretic paragraph mark (פ) closes the chapter.
